The foot is our first point of contact with the ground during running, yet it’s often one of the most overlooked areas in strength training. We prioritize the quads, hamstrings, glutes and calves, but forget about the structures responsible for managing load, adapting to the ground and contributing to force transfer with every stride. Footwear can certainly assist with some of these demands, but passive support isn’t a substitute for developing active strength and control. It’s why I choose shoes like the altrarunning Vanish Pulse for faster runs. Zero drop. Room for natural toe splay. A lower-profile design. That way I can develop the capacity of my feet, rather than only relying on what surrounds them. 🫱🏽‍🫲🏾

videos.caption: Form is the foundation underneath almost every skill you perform. Your balance, speed, power, accuracy, first touch, change of direction and ability to execute under pressure all depend on your body consistently finding the right positions. Good form also requires maintenance. You need enough quality reps that those mechanics remain available when the game gets faster, you're fatigued and pressure increases. Keep these fundamentals sharp: • PASSING: Plant beside the ball, stabilize the ankle, make clean contact and control your follow through. Train both feet and different distances. • RECEIVING: Move your feet early, create the right body angle, stay balanced and direct your touch into the next action. • HALF TURNS: Scan, open your body, adjust your feet and receive from a position that gives you multiple options. • DRIBBLING: Stay athletic over the ball, coordinate touches with your stride and keep the ball within playable distance. • CHANGE OF DIRECTION: Lower your center of gravity, plant under control, redirect your hips and explode into the next movement. • ACCELERATION + DECELERATION: Practice powerful first steps, arm drive and ground contact, then learn to shorten your steps, lower your body and stop under control. • JOCKEYING: Stay low, keep your feet active and manage your distance while remaining balanced enough to react either way. • STRIKING: Repeat your approach, plant foot, ankle position, contact point and follow through before adding more power. • BALL MANIPULATION: V pulls, L drags, turns and inside, outside and sole touches all need exact foot placement and body control. The goal is quality repetition. Those reps protect your mechanics. Your mechanics give you something reliable to build speed, pressure and decision making on top of. The game will eventually test your technique while you're tired, rushed and uncomfortable. That's when your reps need to show. Form first. Quality reps. Keep your fundamentals ready for the game. #coachedbymerv #defender #soccertraining #soccerdrills #soccerskills
